metaDescription: Southwest Sandhill sits near the Monahans Sandhills in Ward County. Get a straight valuation on your mineral or royalty interest here.
heroLead: Southwest Sandhill is an unincorporated community near the dune country west of Monahans, sitting over a mix of old legacy production and newer horizontal acreage typical of Ward County.
intro: The Monahans Sandhills give this part of the county its name and its distinctive terrain, but underground the story is the same layered one you find across Ward County: decades-old vertical leases still held by production, with horizontal Wolfcamp development from the busier Delaware Basin counties to the south extending into some of the surrounding acreage.

sections.heading: Dune country surface, oilfield subsurface
paragraphs: The sandy dune terrain near Southwest Sandhill hasn't stopped drilling here — it's mostly undeveloped surface even where the minerals below have been producing for decades. If your family holds an interest in this area, the terrain itself has little bearing on what the minerals are worth.

sections.heading: Legacy leases with room for a second look
paragraphs: A lot of the leases covering this part of Ward County date back many decades and have simply been held by production on modest vertical wells since. Where newer horizontal units have reached nearby, some of those old leases have seen renewed interest from operators looking to redrill the same acreage more efficiently.

sections.heading: Fractional ownership around the dune country
paragraphs: As with much of Ward County, mineral ownership near Southwest Sandhill often traces back to original ranching allotments that have since split among multiple generations of heirs. It's common to find owners here with interests measured in small fractions of a fraction, sometimes without a clear picture of exactly what they hold or what it might be worth.
We work with a title company to reconstruct ownership from Ward County clerk records, and we can typically purchase your specific undivided share even if you're only one of several heirs.

faqs.question: Does the sandhill terrain limit drilling in this area?
faqs.answer: No. It's mostly undeveloped surface, and horizontal drilling doesn't require developed surface access the way older operations might have. Production has continued in this area for decades.

faqs.question: My family's lease near Southwest Sandhill is decades old. Is it still active?
faqs.answer: Likely, if it's been continuously held by production, which is common in this part of Ward County. We verify this through county clerk records before valuing your interest.

faqs.question: Is there any new drilling activity reaching this area?
faqs.answer: Horizontal development from the busier Delaware Basin counties to the south has been extending into parts of Ward County. We check current permits near your specific tract to confirm.

faqs.question: I only know I have some kind of interest near Southwest Sandhill but not the details. Can you help figure it out?
faqs.answer: Yes. Send us any name, well number, or check stub you have and we'll use Ward County clerk records to trace the ownership and confirm what you actually hold.
